1.explanation:
1. src/ol/layer/Group.js: This is where group-level opacity is propagated into each child’s layerState via getLayerStatesArray (multiplying child opacity by group opacity). If this never reaches vector tile renderers, their labels won’t fade.
2. src/ol/renderer/canvas/VectorTileLayer.js: The canvas-based vector-tile renderer draws text symbols and images but does not apply the layerState.opacity (globalAlpha) when painting labels, so group opacity has no effect on those labels.
3. src/ol/renderer/webgl/VectorTileLayer.js: The WebGL vector-tile renderer must take the layerState.opacity into account (via uniforms.GLOBAL_ALPHA) for text styling as well. If it’s only applied to fill/stroke geometry but not to text symbols, vectortile labels stay fully opaque.
4. src/ol/renderer/Composite.js: The composite renderer composes all layer canvases into a single DOM container. It relies on each layer’s renderer to honor state.opacity. Ensuring group opacity is actually forwarded into the rendered canvas/WebGL draw calls here (or by adding a CSS opacity on the group container) is necessary so that all child layers (including vector-tile labels) participate correctly.
1.bug_scenario: In the CodeSandbox demo, there are two layers in a layer group: a standard vector layer and a vector-tile layer with text labels. Dragging the “vector” or “vectortile” opacity sliders correctly fades in/out that layer’s labels. However, dragging the “group” slider (which calls setOpacity on the layer group) only affects the standard vector layer’s labels. The vector-tile labels (text symbols in canvas or WebGL) remain at full opacity, even though the group’s overall opacity should be applied to all child layers.
